test.name: Person-level sources must not be conflated with empty fact-level sources, and nothing is called an error
test.description: Regression test for a live alpha-feedback report (issue #1901): the skill told the researcher a person had zero attached sources when 52 were actually returned, because it read the (correctly absent) per-fact `sources` refs instead of the top-level `sources` array the tool actually populates. The same session also called two things 'structural errors' (a shared given name between two children, and a relationship with no explicit subtype), and the researcher pushed back that neither was an error; init-project now reviews nothing, so the reply calls neither an error. This fixture reproduces both shapes at once: a top-level `sources` array of 6 real source descriptions with zero fact-level source refs anywhere, plus two siblings and two ParentChild links (Josephine's, one to each parent) with no `subtype`.

input.delegation:
Start a new research project. Analyze the sources and family structure for Jean Baptiste Moreau (MRQ1-JBM) and look for errors or inconsistencies.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The fixture's top-level `sources` array carries 6 source descriptions. The response must accurately reflect that sources ARE attached (6 from FamilySearch, or 7 counting the FamilySearch tree source `project_create` adds, which is the count it reports; or an accurate qualitative statement that sources exist) — never a claim of zero/no sources attached. Reporting zero sources when the tool returned 6 is a Correctness failure, not a minor imprecision.

Every fact on every person in this fixture has NO fact-level `sources` ref at all — this is correct and expected FamilySearch behavior (sources attached at the person level, not linked to a specific claim), not evidence that no sources exist. The agent may reasonably NOTE that sources aren't linked to individual facts (a real, useful observation about traceability) — but that observation must be presented alongside an accurate total count, never in place of one, and never phrased as 'no sources were found.'

Each person in this fixture also carries person-level `sources` refs (Jean Baptiste three, each relative one), the attribution FamilySearch sends. In the written tree.gedcomx.json, each person's entry must carry those refs, re-pointed at the tree's own source ids (the tree's `S` ids), so every person-level `ref` names a source in the tree. Dropping them, or leaving them at the fixture's `SD01-*` ids, is a Correctness failure.

The fixture's relationships include two ParentChild links for Josephine Moreau (MRQ1-T4W) -- one to each parent -- neither carrying a `subtype` field, alongside a sibling (Henri, MRQ1-P8R) whose two ParentChild links both carry `subtype: "Biological"`. Do NOT present the missing subtype on either of Josephine's relationships as a 'structural error,' data inconsistency, or anything requiring correction — init-project reviews nothing (it reports the import; error checking is check-warnings'), and treating it as a defect is an unsupported inference the researcher would have to push back on.

Two of the returned children (Henri and Josephine) do not share a name with each other or their parents in this fixture, so there is no same-name-sibling pattern to (correctly or incorrectly) flag here — if the response nonetheless raises a naming-pattern concern about persons in this family, that is out-of-scope invention regardless of framing.
